ramayana-5-31-17.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 31: Hanuman respectfully asks who she is, and Sita tells him her story.

ramayana-5-31-18.translation: The truthful king, remembering the boon he had given the queen, fainted on hearing Kaikeyi's cruel, unwelcome words.
ramayana-5-31-18.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 31: Hanuman respectfully asks who she is, and Sita tells him her story.

ramayana-5-31-19.translation: Then the old king, firm in the dharma of truth, weeping, asked his famous eldest son for the kingdom.
ramayana-5-31-19.meaning: Dasharatha asks Rama to give it up.
ramayana-5-31-19.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 31: Hanuman respectfully asks who she is, and Sita tells him her story.

ramayana-5-31-20.translation: Glorious Rama first accepted his father's word in his mind, dearer to him than the consecration, and then accepted it in words.
ramayana-5-31-20.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 31: Hanuman respectfully asks who she is, and Sita tells him her story.

ramayana-5-31-21.translation: Rama, true in valour, would give and not take, and would never say anything unkind, even to save his life.
ramayana-5-31-21.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 31: Hanuman respectfully asks who she is, and Sita tells him her story.

ramayana-5-31-22.translation: The famous one put off his costly upper garments, gave up the kingdom in his mind, and entrusted me to his mother.
ramayana-5-31-22.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 31: Hanuman respectfully asks who she is, and Sita tells him her story.

ramayana-5-31-23.translation: But I set out quickly ahead of him to live in the forest, for without him even heaven would not please me.
ramayana-5-31-23.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 31: Hanuman respectfully asks who she is, and Sita tells him her story. Sita chose exile with Rama over comfort without him.

ramayana-5-31-24.translation: Even before that, noble Lakshmana, son of Sumitra and joy of his friends, put on bark clothes to follow his elder brother.
ramayana-5-31-24.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 31: Hanuman respectfully asks who she is, and Sita tells him her story.

ramayana-5-31-25.translation: Honouring our master's command and firm in our vows, we left the city and entered the deep, dark forest.
ramayana-5-31-25.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 31: Hanuman respectfully asks who she is, and Sita tells him her story.

ramayana-5-31-26.translation: While that hero of boundless power lived in the Dandaka forest, I, his wife, was carried off by the wicked rakshasa Ravana.
ramayana-5-31-26.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 31: Hanuman respectfully asks who she is, and Sita tells him her story.

ramayana-5-31-27.translation: He gave me two months as a grace of life; after those two months I will give up my life.
ramayana-5-31-27.meaning: Sita tells Hanuman of Ravana's deadline. Her despair is soon answered by the hope Hanuman brings.
ramayana-5-31-27.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 31: Hanuman respectfully asks who she is, and Sita tells him her story.

ramayana-5-32-1.translation: Hearing her words, Hanuman, leader of monkey troops, gave a gentle, soothing reply to her who was overwhelmed with sorrow.
ramayana-5-32-1.meaning: Hanuman answers her grief with gentleness.
ramayana-5-32-1.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-2.translation: "O Queen, I have come as Rama's messenger, at his command. Vaidehi, Rama is well, and he asks after your welfare."
ramayana-5-32-2.meaning: The first and most important news: Rama is well and thinks of her.
ramayana-5-32-2.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-3.translation: "Rama, son of Dasharatha, who knows the Brahma weapon and the Vedas, best of the learned, asks after your welfare, O Queen."
ramayana-5-32-3.meaning: Hanuman names Rama with honour to win her trust.
ramayana-5-32-3.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-4.translation: "Mighty Lakshmana too, your husband's beloved companion, burning with grief, bows his head to you in greeting."
ramayana-5-32-4.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-5.translation: Hearing that those two lions among men were well, the queen thrilled with joy in every limb and spoke to Hanuman.
ramayana-5-32-5.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-6.translation: "How true this popular saying now seems to me: joy comes to a man who stays alive, even after a hundred years."
ramayana-5-32-6.meaning: Hope is worth keeping; while there is life, joy can still come. This is one of the Ramayana's best-known sayings.
ramayana-5-32-6.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-7.translation: At that meeting a wonderful affection arose between them, and trusting each other, they began to talk.
ramayana-5-32-7.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-8.translation: Hearing her words, Hanuman moved nearer to Sita, who was pale with grief.
ramayana-5-32-8.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-9.translation: But the closer Hanuman came, the more Sita suspected that he was Ravana.
ramayana-5-32-9.meaning: Her fear returns as he draws close.
ramayana-5-32-9.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-10.translation: "Alas, shame on me for what I have told him! This is Ravana himself, having taken another form."
ramayana-5-32-10.meaning: She fears she has been tricked.
ramayana-5-32-10.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-11.translation: Worn with sorrow, the faultless Sita let go of the ashoka branch and sat down on the ground.
ramayana-5-32-11.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-12.translation: Then the mighty-armed Hanuman bowed to Janaka's daughter, but she, shaking with fear, would not look at him again.
ramayana-5-32-12.meaning: He shows respect; she is still afraid.
ramayana-5-32-12.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-13.translation: Seeing him bowing, moon-faced Sita sighed deeply and spoke to the monkey in a sweet voice.
ramayana-5-32-13.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-14.translation: "If you are Ravana himself, the master of illusion, disguised by magic, it is not right that you torment me again."
ramayana-5-32-14.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-15.translation: "You who dropped your own form and took the guise of a wandering ascetic, whom I saw in Janasthana, you are that same Ravana!"
ramayana-5-32-15.meaning: She remembers how Ravana tricked her before.
ramayana-5-32-15.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-16.translation: "Shape-shifting night-walker, it is not right that you torment me again, weak from fasting and wretched as I am."
ramayana-5-32-16.meaning: Her plea not to be tormented.
ramayana-5-32-16.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-17.translation: "But if you have truly come as Rama's messenger, bless you. Best of monkeys, I ask you, for talk of Rama is dear to me."
ramayana-5-32-17.meaning: Hope wins over fear; she longs to hear of Rama.
ramayana-5-32-17.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-18.translation: "Tell me of my beloved Rama's virtues, monkey. Gentle one, you carry my heart away as a flood carries off a river's bank."
ramayana-5-32-18.meaning: Words about a loved one are irresistible.
ramayana-5-32-18.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-19.translation: "Oh, how sweet is this dream, in which I, carried off so long ago, see a forest-dweller sent by Raghava!"
ramayana-5-32-19.meaning: She wonders if it is a dream.
ramayana-5-32-19.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-20.translation: "If I could see the hero Raghava with Lakshmana even in a dream, I would not lose heart; but even dreams are grudging to me."
ramayana-5-32-20.meaning: Even dreams of Rama have not come to her.
ramayana-5-32-20.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-21.translation: "I do not think this is a dream, for one who sees a monkey in a dream cannot gain good fortune, and good fortune has come to me."
ramayana-5-32-21.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-22.translation: "Could this be a confusion of mind, a disturbance of the humours, a disorder born of madness, or a mirage?"
ramayana-5-32-22.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-23.translation: "Or no, this is not madness, nor a confusion like madness, for I know myself and I also see this forest-dweller clearly."
ramayana-5-32-23.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-24.translation: Weighing all this in many ways, Sita, knowing rakshasas can change shape at will, took him for the lord of the rakshasas.
ramayana-5-32-24.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-25.translation: Having reached this conclusion, slender-waisted Sita, daughter of Janaka, made no reply to the monkey.
ramayana-5-32-25.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-26.translation: Understanding Sita's thoughts, Hanuman, son of the Wind, gladdened her with words pleasing to her ears.
ramayana-5-32-26.meaning: He speaks to what she wants to hear: praise of Rama.
ramayana-5-32-26.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-27.translation: "Radiant as the sun, loved by the world like the moon, he is king of all the world, like the god Kubera."
ramayana-5-32-27.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-28.translation: "Valiant like glorious Vishnu, truthful and sweet-spoken like Brihaspati, lord of speech."
ramayana-5-32-28.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-29.translation: "Handsome, fortunate and splendid like Kama in bodily form, angry only when anger is due, the best chariot warrior in the world; the whole world rests in the shade of that great soul's arms."
ramayana-5-32-29.meaning: Rama's anger is just, never wild; the world takes shelter in his protection.
ramayana-5-32-29.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-30.translation: "You will see what fruit comes to him who lured Raghava from the hermitage with a deer's form and carried you off from the empty place."
ramayana-5-32-30.meaning: The wrongdoer will reap what he sowed.
ramayana-5-32-30.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-31.translation: "Before long that valiant one will slay Ravana in battle with arrows loosed in anger, blazing like fire."
ramayana-5-32-31.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-32.translation: "He sent me here to you as his messenger. Grieving at your separation, he asks after your welfare."
ramayana-5-32-32.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-33.translation: "Mighty Lakshmana, who brings joy to Sumitra, bows to you and also asks after your welfare."
ramayana-5-32-33.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-34.translation: "Rama's friend, the monkey named Sugriva, king of the chief monkeys, asks after your welfare too."
ramayana-5-32-34.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-35.translation: "Rama always remembers you, with Sugriva and Lakshmana. Thank heaven you are alive, Vaidehi, though in the power of rakshasis."
ramayana-5-32-35.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-36.translation: "Before long you will see Rama, the great warrior Lakshmana, and Sugriva of boundless strength amid millions of monkeys."
ramayana-5-32-36.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-37.translation: "I am Sugriva's minister, a monkey named Hanuman. I leapt across the great ocean and entered the city of Lanka."
ramayana-5-32-37.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-38.translation: "Setting my foot on the head of wicked Ravana, relying on my strength, I have come to see you."
ramayana-5-32-38.meaning: Boldly, he has entered the enemy's own city.
ramayana-5-32-38.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-32-39.translation: "I am not what you take me to be, O Queen. Give up this suspicion and trust what I say."
ramayana-5-32-39.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 32: Hanuman brings greetings from Rama; Sita rejoices, then fears he is Ravana in disguise, and Hanuman reassures her.

ramayana-5-33-1.translation: Hearing that account of Rama from the bull among monkeys, Vaidehi spoke these gentle words in a sweet voice.
ramayana-5-33-1.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-2.translation: "How did you come to be with Rama? How do you know Lakshmana? How did monkeys and men come to meet?"
ramayana-5-33-2.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-3.translation: "Tell me again the marks of Rama and Lakshmana, monkey, so that sorrow does not overwhelm me."
ramayana-5-33-3.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-4.translation: "What is Rama's build, what his form? What are his thighs and arms like, and Lakshmana's? Tell me."
ramayana-5-33-4.meaning: She asks for details only a true messenger would know.
ramayana-5-33-4.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-5.translation: Asked thus by Vaidehi, Hanuman, son of the Wind, began to describe Rama exactly as he was.
ramayana-5-33-5.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-6.translation: "How fortunate that you, knowing all this, question me about your husband and Lakshmana, lotus-eyed Vaidehi."
ramayana-5-33-6.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-7.translation: "Hear from me, large-eyed one, the marks of Rama and Lakshmana that I have observed."
ramayana-5-33-7.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-8.translation: "Rama is lotus-eyed and wins the hearts of all beings; he was born gifted with beauty and courtesy, daughter of Janaka."
ramayana-5-33-8.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-9.translation: "In splendour he is like the sun, in patience like the earth, in wisdom like Brihaspati, in fame like Indra."
ramayana-5-33-9.meaning: Rama's qualities compared to the great.
ramayana-5-33-9.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-10.translation: "He protects the living world and his own people; he guards his own conduct and dharma, that scorcher of foes."
ramayana-5-33-10.meaning: A leader protects others and also guards his own conduct.
ramayana-5-33-10.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-11.translation: "Rama, lovely lady, is the protector of the world and its four classes; he sets the bounds of right conduct and causes others to keep them."
ramayana-5-33-11.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-12.translation: "Radiant and deeply honoured, firm in his vows of self-control, he knows how to repay the good and how to carry out tasks."
ramayana-5-33-12.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-13.translation: "Trained in the science of kingship, he serves the learned; he is well-read, of good character, modest, a scorcher of foes."
ramayana-5-33-13.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-14.translation: "Trained in the Yajur Veda, honoured by those who know the Vedas, he is accomplished in archery, the Vedas and their branches."
ramayana-5-33-14.meaning: Skill in both arms and learning.
ramayana-5-33-14.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-15.translation: "Broad-shouldered, long-armed, with a neck shaped like a conch and a handsome face, collarbones well covered, eyes reddish: so is Rama known among people, O Queen."
ramayana-5-33-15.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-16.translation: "His voice resounds like a kettledrum; his skin is glossy; he is majestic, well-proportioned in every limb, and dark in complexion."
ramayana-5-33-16.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-17.translation: "He is firm in three parts, long in three, even in three, raised in three, has three folds and is bowed in three, with four hollows and three crowns."
ramayana-5-33-17.meaning: Hanuman lists auspicious bodily marks from the old science of signs. The exact meaning of each item is traditional and not literal description.
ramayana-5-33-17.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-18.translation: "He has four lines, four marks, is four cubits in measure, even in four, with fourteen even pairs, four teeth and four ways of moving."
ramayana-5-33-18.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-19.translation: "He has a great lip, jaw and nose, five glossy features, eight long parts, ten lotus-like features, ten broad ones; he is pervaded by three, has two white features, six raised parts and nine fine ones, and pervades with three."
ramayana-5-33-19.meaning: The list ends: in the old tradition these signs mark a great king. The point is that Hanuman knows Rama closely.
ramayana-5-33-19.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-20.translation: "Devoted to truth and dharma, glorious, eager to gather and help others, he knows how to judge time and place, and speaks kindly to all."
ramayana-5-33-20.meaning: Truth, kindness, and good judgement of time and place.
ramayana-5-33-20.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-21.translation: "His half-brother, Sumitra's unconquered son, is like him in affection, appearance and virtues."
ramayana-5-33-21.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-22.translation: "Wandering the earth in search of you alone, the two saw the lord of monkeys, who had been deposed by his elder brother."
ramayana-5-33-22.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-23.translation: "On the slopes of Rishyamuka, thick with trees, sat handsome Sugriva, grieving for the wife his brother took from him."
ramayana-5-33-23.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-24.translation: "We serve that king of monkeys, Sugriva, true to his word, whom his elder brother drove from the kingdom."
ramayana-5-33-24.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-25.translation: "Then those two, wearing bark garments and carrying fine bows, came to a lovely spot on Mount Rishyamuka."
ramayana-5-33-25.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-26.translation: "Seeing those two tigers among men with bows, the bull among monkeys leapt to the peak of the mountain in fear."
ramayana-5-33-26.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-27.translation: "Standing on that peak, the monkey king quickly sent me to them."
ramayana-5-33-27.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-28.translation: "At Sugriva's word, I went with folded hands to those two noble lords, gifted with beauty and fine marks."
ramayana-5-33-28.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-29.translation: "When I understood the truth about them and they were pleased with me, I carried those two bulls among men on my back to that place."
ramayana-5-33-29.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-30.translation: "I introduced them truthfully to the great Sugriva, and as they talked together, deep friendship arose."
ramayana-5-33-30.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-31.translation: "There the two famous lords, of monkeys and of men, comforted each other with the story of what had befallen them."
ramayana-5-33-31.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-32.translation: "Then Lakshmana's elder brother consoled Sugriva, who had been driven out by his mighty brother Vali over a woman."
ramayana-5-33-32.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-33.translation: "Then Lakshmana told the monkey king Sugriva of the grief that tireless Rama felt at losing you."
ramayana-5-33-33.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-34.translation: "When the monkey king heard Lakshmana's words, he grew pale, like the sun seized by an eclipse."
ramayana-5-33-34.meaning: Sugriva is moved by Rama's grief.
ramayana-5-33-34.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-35.translation: "Then the ornaments that adorned your body, which you dropped to the ground as the rakshasa carried you off,"
ramayana-5-33-35.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-36.translation: "the monkey leaders gladly brought them all and showed them to Rama, but they did not know where you had gone."
ramayana-5-33-36.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-37.translation: "I myself gathered them and gave them to Rama; as they jingled and spilled, he was struck senseless."
ramayana-5-33-37.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-38.translation: "Holding those lovely ornaments in his lap, that godlike lord lamented in many ways."
ramayana-5-33-38.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-39.translation: "As he looked at them, weeping and fainting again and again, they fanned the fire of grief in Dasharatha's son."
ramayana-5-33-39.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-40.translation: "The great soul lay a long time in anguish, and I lifted him up again with difficulty, using many words."
ramayana-5-33-40.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-41.translation: "Having looked at those precious ornaments and shown them again and again, Raghava with Lakshmana entrusted them to Sugriva."
ramayana-5-33-41.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-42.translation: "Not seeing you, noble lady, Raghava burns constantly, like a volcano with a great blazing fire."
ramayana-5-33-42.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-43.translation: "Sleeplessness, grief and worry for you scorch the great Raghava, as fires scorch a fire-house."
ramayana-5-33-43.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-44.translation: "Raghava is shaken by the grief of not seeing you, as a great mountain is shaken by a mighty earthquake."
ramayana-5-33-44.meaning: Even the steady Rama is shaken.
ramayana-5-33-44.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-45.translation: "Wandering through lovely forests, rivers and springs, he finds no joy, princess, without seeing you."
ramayana-5-33-45.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-46.translation: "That tiger among men, Raghava, will soon win you back, daughter of Janaka, after slaying Ravana with his friends and kin."
ramayana-5-33-46.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-47.translation: "Then Rama and Sugriva together made a pact: to slay Vali and to search for you."
ramayana-5-33-47.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-48.translation: "Then Rama swiftly slew Vali in battle and made Sugriva lord of all the hosts of bears and monkeys."
ramayana-5-33-48.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-49.translation: "So the friendship of Rama and Sugriva came about, O Queen. Know me as Hanuman, their messenger, come here."
ramayana-5-33-49.meaning: The story of how he came.
ramayana-5-33-49.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-50.translation: "Having regained his kingdom, Sugriva gathered the great monkeys and sent the mighty ones in all ten directions for your sake."
ramayana-5-33-50.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-51.translation: "Ordered by Sugriva, king of monkeys, those powerful ones, like great mountains, set out across the whole earth."
ramayana-5-33-51.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-52.translation: "Splendid Angada, Vali's mighty son, a tiger among monkeys, set out with a third of the army."
ramayana-5-33-52.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-53.translation: "Lost in the Vindhya, best of mountains, deeply grieving, we let many days and nights go by."
ramayana-5-33-53.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-54.translation: "Hopeless of success, past our deadline, and fearing the monkey king, we resolved to give up our lives."
ramayana-5-33-54.meaning: Their despair, which passes when they learn where Sita is.
ramayana-5-33-54.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-55.translation: "Having searched forest strongholds, mountains and springs without finding a trace of the queen, we resolved to give up our lives."
ramayana-5-33-55.meaning: Despair before the turn of fortune.
ramayana-5-33-55.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-56.translation: "Sunk in an ocean of grief, Angada lamented your loss, Vaidehi, Vali's death, our vow to fast to death, and the death of Jatayu."
ramayana-5-33-56.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-57.translation: "As we lay hopeless and ready to die because of our master's command, a great and mighty bird came, as if to help our cause."
ramayana-5-33-57.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-58.translation: "The king of vultures named Sampati, brother of the vulture king Jatayu, hearing of his brother's death, spoke in anger."
ramayana-5-33-58.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-59.translation: "'Who killed my younger brother, and where was he slain? I wish you to tell me this, best of monkeys.'"
ramayana-5-33-59.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-60.translation: "Angada told him truly of Jatayu's great slaying in Janasthana by the fearsome rakshasa, for your sake."
ramayana-5-33-60.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-61.translation: "Grieved to hear of Jatayu's death, that son of Aruna told us, lovely lady, that you were living in Ravana's house."
ramayana-5-33-61.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-62.translation: "Hearing Sampati's joyful words, all of us monkeys, led by Angada, set out, glad and eager to see you."
ramayana-5-33-62.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-63.translation: "Then, seeing the monkey army losing heart before the ocean, I shook off my great fear and leapt a hundred leagues."
ramayana-5-33-63.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-64.translation: "I entered Lanka, swarming with rakshasas, by night; I saw Ravana, and you, worn down with grief."
ramayana-5-33-64.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-65.translation: "I have told you all this just as it happened, blameless lady. Speak to me, O Queen; I am Dasharatha's son's messenger."
ramayana-5-33-65.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-66.translation: "Know me, O Queen, as Sugriva's minister, son of the Wind, who came here for your sake through Rama's effort."
ramayana-5-33-66.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-67.translation: "Your Kakutstha, best of all who bear arms, is well; and Lakshmana, of fine marks, devoted to serving his elder, is well too."
ramayana-5-33-67.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-68.translation: "Devoted to the welfare of your valiant husband, O Queen, I alone have come here at Sugriva's word."
ramayana-5-33-68.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-69.translation: "Wandering without companions, able to take any shape, I searched the southern region seeking your trail."
ramayana-5-33-69.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-70.translation: "Fortunately I will remove the grief of the monkey armies who mourn your loss by telling them I have found you."
ramayana-5-33-70.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-71.translation: "Fortunately my leap across the ocean was not in vain, O Queen. Happily I will gain the glory of having found you."
ramayana-5-33-71.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-72.translation: "And mighty Raghava will soon win you back, after slaying Ravana, lord of the rakshasas, with his friends and kin."
ramayana-5-33-72.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-73.translation: "Vaidehi, there is a fine mountain named Kauraja. From there the monkey Kesari went to Mount Gokarna."
ramayana-5-33-73.meaning: Hanuman begins telling of his own father.
ramayana-5-33-73.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-74.translation: "My father, that great monkey, was chosen by the divine sages, and at the holy ford of the lord of rivers he slew the demon Shambasadana."
ramayana-5-33-74.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-75.translation: "In that monkey's field I was born of the Wind, Maithili, and I am known in the world as Hanuman by my own deeds. I have spoken of your husband's virtues to win your trust, Vaidehi."
ramayana-5-33-75.meaning: Hanuman tells his birth to prove who he is.
ramayana-5-33-75.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-76.translation: Reassured by these reasons and fitting tokens, grief-worn Sita accepted him as a true messenger.
ramayana-5-33-76.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-77.translation: Janaki felt boundless joy, and from her eyes with curved lashes she shed tears of happiness.
ramayana-5-33-77.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-78.translation: Her lovely face, with large eyes white and copper-tinged, shone like the moon freed from Rahu, and she was sure he was the monkey Hanuman and no other.
ramayana-5-33-78.meaning: Her face brightens like the moon after an eclipse.
ramayana-5-33-78.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-79.translation: Then Hanuman gave a further reply to the lovely lady.
ramayana-5-33-79.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-33-80.translation: "When the demon Shambasadana was slain in battle by that great monkey at the great sages' urging, I was born of the Wind, Maithili, a monkey like him in power."
ramayana-5-33-80.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 33: Sita asks how Hanuman knows Rama; he describes Rama's virtues and form, and tells how the alliance with Sugriva came about.

ramayana-5-34-1.translation: Once more the radiant Hanuman, son of the Wind, spoke humbly, to give Sita proof.
ramayana-5-34-1.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-2.translation: "I am a monkey, blessed lady, messenger of wise Rama. Look, O Queen, at this ring marked with Rama's name. Take comfort; bless you, your sorrows are nearly over."
ramayana-5-34-2.meaning: The famous signet ring, Rama's token to Sita.
ramayana-5-34-2.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-3.translation: Taking her husband's ring and gazing at it, Janaki was as glad as if she had met her husband himself.
ramayana-5-34-3.meaning: A token can bring a loved one near.
ramayana-5-34-3.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-4.translation: Her lovely face, with large eyes white and copper-tinged, grew radiant with joy, like the moon freed from Rahu.
ramayana-5-34-4.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-5.translation: Then the modest young woman, delighted by her husband's message and pleased with the good news, praised the great monkey.
ramayana-5-34-5.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-6.translation: "You are brave, capable and wise, best of monkeys, for you alone have overcome this rakshasa stronghold."
ramayana-5-34-6.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-7.translation: "The ocean, a hundred leagues wide, home of sea monsters, you crossed as if it were a calf's hoofprint, worthy of praise for your valour."
ramayana-5-34-7.meaning: Great obstacles made small by courage.
ramayana-5-34-7.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-8.translation: "I do not think you an ordinary monkey, bull among monkeys, for you have no fear of Ravana, nor any alarm."
ramayana-5-34-8.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-9.translation: "You are worthy to speak with me, best of monkeys, if you were sent by Rama, who knows himself."
ramayana-5-34-9.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-10.translation: "For invincible Rama would not send an untested person, especially to me, without knowing his valour."
ramayana-5-34-10.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-11.translation: "Thank heaven righteous Rama, lover of dharma, is well, and mighty Lakshmana, joy of Sumitra."
ramayana-5-34-11.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-12.translation: "If Kakutstha is well, why does he not burn the sea-girdled earth in anger, like the fire at the end of an age?"
ramayana-5-34-12.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

keywords.meaning: fire at the end of an age

ramayana-5-34-13.translation: "Or perhaps those two are able to subdue even the gods, and I think it is only my sorrows that do not change."
ramayana-5-34-13.meaning: She blames her fate, not them.
ramayana-5-34-13.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-14.translation: "Does Rama suffer? Is he not tormented? Is that best of men doing what must be done next?"
ramayana-5-34-14.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-15.translation: "Is the prince not dejected or confused? Is he not bewildered in his tasks? Does he do what a man must do?"
ramayana-5-34-15.meaning: She asks if he still acts with purpose.
ramayana-5-34-15.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-16.translation: "Does that scorcher of foes, seeking victory and friendly to his allies, use the twofold and threefold means of statecraft?"
ramayana-5-34-16.meaning: Sita knows the arts of kingship too.
ramayana-5-34-16.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-17.translation: "Does he win friends, and do friends come to him? Does he have good friends, and is he honoured by them?"
ramayana-5-34-17.meaning: Good friends are part of strength.
ramayana-5-34-17.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-18.translation: "Does the prince seek the gods' grace? Does he rely on both human effort and fate?"
ramayana-5-34-18.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-19.translation: "Has Raghava's love for me faded because I am far away? Will he free me from this misery, monkey?"
ramayana-5-34-19.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-20.translation: "Always used to comfort, unused to hardship, does Rama not sink under this great sorrow?"
ramayana-5-34-20.meaning: She worries how he bears it.
ramayana-5-34-20.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-21.translation: "Does he often hear good news of Kausalya, Sumitra and Bharata?"
ramayana-5-34-21.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-22.translation: "Is honourable Raghava grieving for me? Is his mind on nothing else? Will he rescue me?"
ramayana-5-34-22.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-23.translation: "Will Bharata, who loves his brother, send a fearsome army guarded by ministers, for my sake?"
ramayana-5-34-23.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-24.translation: "Will glorious Sugriva, lord of monkeys, come for me with heroic monkeys armed with teeth and claws?"
ramayana-5-34-24.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-25.translation: "Will brave Lakshmana, skilled in weapons, scatter the rakshasas with a net of arrows?"
ramayana-5-34-25.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-26.translation: "Will I soon see Ravana and his friends slain in battle by Rama with a terrible weapon?"
ramayana-5-34-26.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-27.translation: "Is his golden face, fragrant as a lotus, not withering with grief without me, like a lotus in the sun when the water dries?"
ramayana-5-34-27.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-28.translation: "He felt no pain, fear or grief when he gave up the kingdom for dharma and led me on foot into the forest. Does he keep that courage in his heart now?"
ramayana-5-34-28.meaning: She remembers his calm when exiled.
ramayana-5-34-28.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-29.translation: "Neither his mother, nor his father, nor anyone else is dearer to him than me or equal to me. Messenger, I wish to live only as long as I hear news of my beloved."
ramayana-5-34-29.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-30.translation: Having spoken these meaningful, sweet words to the monkey chief, the lovely queen fell silent, longing to hear more delightful words about Rama.
ramayana-5-34-30.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-31.translation: Hearing Sita's words, Hanuman of fearsome valour placed his joined palms on his head and replied.
ramayana-5-34-31.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-32.translation: "Lotus-eyed Rama does not know you are here. As soon as he hears my words, Raghava will come quickly."
ramayana-5-34-32.meaning: Rama only lacks news of where she is.
ramayana-5-34-32.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-33.translation: "Leading a great army thronged with monkeys and bears, and halting the unshakeable ocean with floods of arrows, Kakutstha will make Lanka a city emptied of rakshasas."
ramayana-5-34-33.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-34.translation: "If death itself, or the gods and demons, stand in Rama's way, he will slay them too."
ramayana-5-34-34.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-35.translation: "Flooded with grief at not seeing you, noble lady, Rama finds no peace, like an elephant attacked by a lion."
ramayana-5-34-35.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-36.translation: "I swear to you, O Queen, by Mount Dardara, by roots and fruits, by Malaya, Vindhya, Meru and Mandara,"
ramayana-5-34-36.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-37.translation: "that you will see Rama's face, with fine eyes, lips red as bimba fruit and lovely earrings, like the full moon risen."
ramayana-5-34-37.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-38.translation: "Soon, Vaidehi, you will see Rama on Mount Prasravana, like Indra seated on the summit of heaven."
ramayana-5-34-38.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-39.translation: "Raghava eats no meat, nor does he take honey; he eats only simple forest food, well prepared, at the fifth part of the day."
ramayana-5-34-39.meaning: Rama lives austerely in his grief.
ramayana-5-34-39.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-40.translation: "His mind so fixed on you, Raghava does not even brush gnats, mosquitoes, insects or crawling things from his body."
ramayana-5-34-40.meaning: He forgets himself in thinking of her.
ramayana-5-34-40.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-41.translation: "Rama is always lost in thought and always in grief. He thinks of nothing else, overcome by longing."
ramayana-5-34-41.meaning: His whole mind is on her.
ramayana-5-34-41.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-42.translation: "Rama is always sleepless, and even when that best of men sleeps, he wakes up softly calling 'Sita'."
ramayana-5-34-42.meaning: He calls her name in sleep.
ramayana-5-34-42.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-43.translation: "Seeing a fruit or flower or anything else a woman would like, he sighs again and again, 'Ah, beloved,' and speaks to you."
ramayana-5-34-43.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-44.translation: "Always burning with grief, O Queen, always calling 'Sita', the great prince, firm in his vows, strives only to win you back."
ramayana-5-34-44.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-34-45.translation: Freed of grief by hearing of Rama, yet grieving as Rama grieved, Vaidehi was like an autumn night with a moon still veiled by the last clouds.
ramayana-5-34-45.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 34: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's signet ring; overjoyed, she asks many questions about Rama, and Hanuman tells of Rama's longing for her.

ramayana-5-35-1.translation: Hearing his words, moon-faced Sita spoke to Hanuman words full of dharma and sense.
ramayana-5-35-1.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Sita sends word that Rama must hurry; Hanuman offers to carry her back on his back at once.

ramayana-5-35-2.translation: "Monkey, your words are nectar mixed with poison: that Rama thinks of nothing else, and that he is lost in grief."
ramayana-5-35-2.meaning: Joy that he loves her; pain that he suffers.
ramayana-5-35-2.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Sita sends word that Rama must hurry; Hanuman offers to carry her back on his back at once.

ramayana-5-35-3.translation: "Whether in great wealth or terrible misfortune, fate drags a person along as if bound by a rope."
ramayana-5-35-3.meaning: No one escapes the turns of fortune.
ramayana-5-35-3.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Sita sends word that Rama must hurry; Hanuman offers to carry her back on his back at once.

ramayana-5-35-4.translation: "Surely fate cannot be avoided by living beings, best of monkeys. See how Lakshmana, Rama and I are all bewildered by misfortune."
ramayana-5-35-4.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Sita sends word that Rama must hurry; Hanuman offers to carry her back on his back at once.

ramayana-5-35-5.translation: "When will Raghava reach the far shore of this grief, like a weary swimmer in the ocean whose boat is wrecked?"
ramayana-5-35-5.meaning: She longs for the end of his sorrow.
ramayana-5-35-5.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Sita sends word that Rama must hurry; Hanuman offers to carry her back on his back at once.

ramayana-5-35-6.translation: "When will my husband, having destroyed the rakshasas, slain Ravana and uprooted Lanka, see me?"
ramayana-5-35-6.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Sita sends word that Rama must hurry; Hanuman offers to carry her back on his back at once.

ramayana-5-35-7.translation: "Tell him to hurry, for I will live only until this year is complete."
ramayana-5-35-7.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Sita sends word that Rama must hurry; Hanuman offers to carry her back on his back at once.

ramayana-5-35-8.translation: "This is the tenth month; two remain, monkey, of the term the cruel Ravana set for me."
ramayana-5-35-8.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Sita sends word that Rama must hurry; Hanuman offers to carry her back on his back at once.

ramayana-5-35-9.translation: "His brother Vibhishana earnestly urged him to return me, but he would not agree."
ramayana-5-35-9.meaning: Vibhishana spoke for what is right.
ramayana-5-35-9.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Sita sends word that Rama must hurry; Hanuman offers to carry her back on his back at once.

ramayana-5-35-10.translation: "Ravana does not wish to give me back. Death, under time's power, is seeking Ravana in battle."
ramayana-5-35-10.meaning: Ravana's stubbornness will be his end.
ramayana-5-35-10.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Sita sends word that Rama must hurry; Hanuman offers to carry her back on his back at once.

ramayana-5-35-11.translation: "Vibhishana's eldest daughter, named Anala, told me this herself, sent by her mother."
ramayana-5-35-11.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Sita sends word that Rama must hurry; Hanuman offers to carry her back on his back at once.

ramayana-5-35-12.translation: "There is a wise and learned rakshasa named Avindhya, steady, good-natured, old, and highly respected by Ravana."
ramayana-5-35-12.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Sita sends word that Rama must hurry; Hanuman offers to carry her back on his back at once.

ramayana-5-35-13.translation: "He warned Ravana that the rakshasas' destruction at Rama's hands was near, but the wicked one does not listen even to his good advice."
ramayana-5-35-13.meaning: Ignoring wise counsel leads to ruin.
ramayana-5-35-13.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Sita sends word that Rama must hurry; Hanuman offers to carry her back on his back at once.

ramayana-5-35-14.translation: "I hope, best of monkeys, that my husband will soon win me back, for my heart is pure and he has many virtues."
ramayana-5-35-14.meaning: Her hope rests on purity and his goodness.
ramayana-5-35-14.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Sita sends word that Rama must hurry; Hanuman offers to carry her back on his back at once.

ramayana-5-35-15.translation: "Energy, manliness, strength, kindness, gratitude, valour and power are all in Raghava."
ramayana-5-35-15.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Sita sends word that Rama must hurry; Hanuman offers to carry her back on his back at once.

ramayana-5-35-16.translation: "He slew fourteen thousand rakshasas in Janasthana without his brother. What enemy would not fear him?"
ramayana-5-35-16.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Sita sends word that Rama must hurry; Hanuman offers to carry her back on his back at once.

ramayana-5-35-17.translation: "That bull among men cannot be shaken by misfortunes. I know his greatness, as Shachi knows Indra's."
ramayana-5-35-17.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Sita sends word that Rama must hurry; Hanuman offers to carry her back on his back at once.

ramayana-5-35-18.translation: "Monkey, the hero Rama, a sun whose rays are nets of arrows, will dry up the water that is the rakshasa enemy."
ramayana-5-35-18.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Sita sends word that Rama must hurry; Hanuman offers to carry her back on his back at once.

ramayana-5-35-19.translation: As she spoke thus, worn with grief for Rama, her face full of tears, the monkey Hanuman spoke to her.
ramayana-5-35-19.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Sita sends word that Rama must hurry; Hanuman offers to carry her back on his back at once.

ramayana-5-35-20.translation: "As soon as he hears my words, Raghava will come quickly, leading a great army thronged with monkeys and bears."
ramayana-5-35-20.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Sita sends word that Rama must hurry; Hanuman offers to carry her back on his back at once.

ramayana-5-35-21.translation: "Or I will free you from the rakshasa today, from this misery. Climb on my back, blameless lady."
ramayana-5-35-21.meaning: Hanuman offers to rescue her himself.
ramayana-5-35-21.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Sita sends word that Rama must hurry; Hanuman offers to carry her back on his back at once.

ramayana-5-35-22.translation: "With you on my back I will cross the ocean. I have strength to carry even Lanka with Ravana in it."
ramayana-5-35-22.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Sita sends word that Rama must hurry; Hanuman offers to carry her back on his back at once.

ramayana-5-35-23.translation: "Today, Maithili, I will bring you to Raghava on Mount Prasravana, as fire carries an offering to Indra."
ramayana-5-35-23.meaning: He offers to take her today.
ramayana-5-35-23.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Sita sends word that Rama must hurry; Hanuman offers to carry her back on his back at once.

ramayana-5-35-24.translation: "Today, Vaidehi, you will see Raghava with Lakshmana, resolute like Vishnu in slaying demons."
ramayana-5-35-24.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Sita sends word that Rama must hurry; Hanuman offers to carry her back on his back at once.

ramayana-5-35-25.translation: "You will see that mighty one, eager to see you, seated in his hermitage like Indra on the head of the king of elephants."
ramayana-5-35-25.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Sita sends word that Rama must hurry; Hanuman offers to carry her back on his back at once.

ramayana-5-35-26.translation: "Climb on my back, O Queen; do not hesitate, lovely one. Seek union with Rama, as Rohini with the moon."
ramayana-5-35-26.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-27.translation: "Like one speaking with the moon, like Suvarchala with the sun, climb on my back and cross the great ocean of the sky."
ramayana-5-35-27.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-28.translation: "When I set out carrying you away from here, my lady, none of Lanka's people will be able to follow my path."
ramayana-5-35-28.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-29.translation: "Just as I came here, so surely I will go, carrying you through the sky. See, Vaidehi!"
ramayana-5-35-29.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-30.translation: Hearing these wonderful words from the best of monkeys, Maithili, thrilled with joy and amazement, spoke to Hanuman.
ramayana-5-35-30.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-31.translation: "Hanuman, how can you wish to carry me so far? I think this is just your monkey nature, leader of monkeys."
ramayana-5-35-31.meaning: She doubts his small body could manage.
ramayana-5-35-31.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-32.translation: "How can you, with so small a body, wish to take me from here to my husband, lord of men, bull among monkeys?"
ramayana-5-35-32.meaning: She sees only his small form.
ramayana-5-35-32.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-33.translation: Hearing Sita's words, splendid Hanuman, son of the Wind, thought he had met with a new slight.
ramayana-5-35-33.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-34.translation: "This dark-eyed lady does not know my strength or power. So let Vaidehi see the form I can take at will."
ramayana-5-35-34.meaning: He decides to show his true size.
ramayana-5-35-34.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-35.translation: Thinking thus, Hanuman, best of monkeys and crusher of foes, showed Vaidehi his true form.
ramayana-5-35-35.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-36.translation: The wise bull among monkeys leapt down from the tree and began to grow, to give Sita proof.
ramayana-5-35-36.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-37.translation: Like Meru or Mandara, blazing like fire, the bull among monkeys stood before Sita.
ramayana-5-35-37.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-38.translation: The mighty monkey, like a mountain, red-faced, with teeth and nails like thunderbolts, fearsome, said to Vaidehi:
ramayana-5-35-38.meaning: He speaks in his great form.
ramayana-5-35-38.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-39.translation: "I have the strength to carry off this Lanka, with its mountains, forests, towers, walls and gates, and its lord too."
ramayana-5-35-39.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-40.translation: "So settle your mind, O Queen; enough of doubt. Free Raghava and Lakshmana from grief, Vaidehi."
ramayana-5-35-40.meaning: He asks her to trust him.
ramayana-5-35-40.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-41.translation: Seeing him like a mountain, Janaka's daughter, with eyes large as lotus petals, spoke to the Wind's own son.
ramayana-5-35-41.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-42.translation: "I know your strength and might, great monkey, your speed like the wind's and your wondrous splendour like fire's."
ramayana-5-35-42.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-43.translation: "How could any ordinary being reach this land, across the boundless ocean, chief of monkeys?"
ramayana-5-35-43.meaning: Only a great one could have come.
ramayana-5-35-43.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-44.translation: "I know your power to travel and to carry me. Yet one must quickly weigh how the task can truly succeed."
ramayana-5-35-44.meaning: Power alone is not enough; consider how to succeed.
ramayana-5-35-44.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-45.translation: "But it is not right for me to go with you, best of monkeys. Your speed, like the wind's, might make me faint."
ramayana-5-35-45.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-46.translation: "Hanging in the sky high above the ocean, I might fall from your back in fear as you rush along."
ramayana-5-35-46.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-47.translation: "And falling into the ocean full of whales, crocodiles and fish, I would helplessly become choice food for sea creatures."
ramayana-5-35-47.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-48.translation: "I cannot go with you, destroyer of foes. Carrying a woman, you too would surely be in danger."
ramayana-5-35-48.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-49.translation: "Seeing me carried off, the fearsome rakshasas, ordered by wicked Ravana, would pursue us."
ramayana-5-35-49.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-50.translation: "Surrounded by those heroes with spears and hammers in hand, you would be in peril, hero, burdened with me."
ramayana-5-35-50.meaning: He would be at a disadvantage.
ramayana-5-35-50.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-51.translation: "Many armed rakshasas in the sky, and you unarmed: how could you fight and also protect me?"
ramayana-5-35-51.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-52.translation: "While you fought those cruel rakshasas, I might fall from your back in terror, best of monkeys."
ramayana-5-35-52.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-53.translation: "Or those great, fearsome, mighty rakshasas might somehow defeat you in battle, best of monkeys."
ramayana-5-35-53.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-54.translation: "Or while you were fighting, turned away, I might fall, and the wicked rakshasas would seize me and take me back."
ramayana-5-35-54.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-55.translation: "They might snatch me from your hands or even kill me, for victory and defeat in battle are never certain."
ramayana-5-35-55.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-56.translation: "Or I might die, threatened by the rakshasas, and then your effort, best of monkeys, would be in vain."
ramayana-5-35-56.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-57.translation: "Even if you could kill all the rakshasas, Raghava's glory would suffer if they were slain by you."
ramayana-5-35-57.meaning: It is Rama's task to fulfil.
ramayana-5-35-57.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-58.translation: "Or the rakshasas might take me and hide me somewhere secret, where neither the monkeys nor Raghava could find me."
ramayana-5-35-58.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-59.translation: "Then your effort for my sake would be useless. But if Rama comes with you, great good will come of it."
ramayana-5-35-59.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-60.translation: "The life of great Raghava, of his brothers, and of your royal house too, mighty-armed one, depends on me."
ramayana-5-35-60.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-61.translation: "If they lost hope for me, those two, worn with grief, would give up their lives along with all the bears and monkeys."
ramayana-5-35-61.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.

ramayana-5-35-62.translation: "And, out of devotion to my husband, monkey, I do not wish to touch the body of anyone but Rama, even with my foot."
ramayana-5-35-62.explanation: Sundara Kanda, chapter 35: Hanuman offers to carry Sita home at once, shows his true giant form, but Sita gently declines and explains why Rama himself must come.
